Definition: from G2596 and G2038; to work fully, i.e. accomplish; by implication, to finish, fashion:--cause, to (deed), perform, work (out).
BiblicalUsage: To work fully is to accomplish, and Paul says sin wrought in him all manner of concupiscence by the commandment, and asks whether the good became death to him, and then says to work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, and godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation. The word holds both the working of sin and the working of salvation, and the difference is who is doing the work and to what end.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sin works death in me and God works salvation in me, and the two workings are at war in the same heart. I hold that I work out what God works in, because my salvation is His work first and my obedience second.
